## Campaign rules (hypothesis.md, verbatim)

### Target buyer persona

- **Titles that buy or decide** (B pulls these; A ranks connections by them):
  - **Founder / CEO / Managing Director / Owner / Director** of an online pharmacy, an online prescriber or a pharmacy group. At most companies here (independent groups and small online pharmacies) the owner decides; at funded online brands the CEO or founder decides with the clinical lead.
  - **Superintendent Pharmacist / Chief Pharmacist / Deputy Chief Pharmacist / Pharmacy Director / Head of Pharmacy.** The superintendent carries GPhC accountability for the registered pharmacy and owns whether the verification step stands up.
  - **Medical Director / Clinical Director / Chief Medical Officer / Head of Clinical Services / Head of Weight Management / lead prescriber.** Owns the prescribing protocol and what an estimate may be used for.
  - **COO / Head of Operations / Head of Patient Onboarding / Head of Consultations.** Owns the review workload: photos and videos checked by eye, video calls, retakes.
  - **CPO / CTO / Head of Product / Head of Digital / Product Manager.** Owns where the step sits in the consultation or checkout flow and the SDK integration.
- **Why these titles:** the superintendent is the one title a generic health-tech list misses and the one the GPhC holds to account; owners decide at small and mid-size pharmacies; clinical leads own the protocol; operations owns the manual review cost; product owns placement. Every IN account also gets a route-in below C-level where one exists (head of pharmacy, clinical lead, prescriber, head of weight management, pharmacy manager), following PPL-1.
- **What they care about (KPIs):** a verification step that stands up under GPhC scrutiny; manual review time per patient (photos, videos, video calls); approval speed and checkout drop-off; audit-readiness of the record; for branch groups, follow-up without a visit.
- **Objections they likely have, with the honest answer:**
  - "An estimate is not a measured weight." True. Smart Scales is a software estimate, not a scale reading. The pharmacy sets its own mismatch threshold and reviews flagged cases; nothing is auto-decided. No accuracy figure is given until R&D publishes the weight baseline (`roadmap.md`); a reply asking for one is offered the meeting or a call.
  - "We already ask for photos, a video of the scales or a video call." Those help. The scan makes the capture itself in-session, adds a predicted-weight cross-check against the declared figure and returns one structured, timestamped record, so the reviewer reads a record and the flagged cases instead of judging every image by eye.
  - "Will it add friction?" Under 45 seconds from the photos to structured results; the pharmacy chooses where the step sits and keeps its current route for anyone who does not scan.
  - "We see patients face to face." The pharmacy keeps that; the scan is a remote option between visits or for an online route.
  - "Where is the data?" AWS, primarily US-West-2, partly US-East-1; no UK residency offer. GDPR controller and processor roles, a DPA with SCCs and a UK Addendum; documents through legal@3dlook.me. Replies only, never cold copy.
  - "Is it a medical device, does it decide eligibility?" FitXpress is not a medical device and does not make eligibility decisions; the pharmacy's clinicians do.
- **Not the buyer:** growth and performance marketing, CRM, retail store, beauty, grocery, wholesale and logistics roles, and dispensing staff with no service remit. B never pulls them. In A they are a `referral` at lowest priority when they work in the pharmacy, online doctor or clinical side of the company, and a FAIL when they work in a retail, beauty, grocery or wholesale line (Superdrug, Asda, Well and Rowlands stores; see Exclusions). Anyone located outside the UK is a FAIL.

### Anti-cases (where it does NOT work)

- **NHS trusts and NHS weight-management services:** different procurement and governance; not this profile's cold-outbound market.
- **Coaching or behavioural weight-loss apps with no medication track** (no prescribing, no eligibility step to defend).
- **Supplement and DTC wellness brands** with no prescribing.
- **GP services and general online pharmacies with no weight-loss service** (no GLP-1 eligibility step): Livi, Push Doctor, Welzo, Care Quality Pharmacy.
- **White-label platforms, fulfilment-only pharmacies and partner services** that do not own the patient's eligibility step (Evaro, Primed Pharmacy, Automeds): partners, not buyers.
- **Comparison, affiliate and price-check sites:** they do not prescribe.
- **Aesthetic or cosmetic clinics** that do not prescribe GLP-1.
- **Non-UK operators**, and non-UK teams of UK groups.
- **Existing customers and the companies Katerina contacts herself** (decision 4).
- **Recent mergers and acquisitions** (`icp-detail.md` universal exclusion) do not exclude here: Vadim kept every company without a contract (decisions 5 and 8). Copy never mentions a deal (Account facts Never lines for Doctor Care Anywhere, Juniper and Avicenna).

## What past campaigns taught (learnings.md 2026-10-30, verbatim)

Campaign rules above win over these. `[directional]` is the default; say why when you depart from it. `[watch]` is not a rule yet.

### People

**PPL-1 [directional] Seniority runs backwards.** C-level and founders replied to 5/344
invites, everyone below them to 37/1064. The validator's P1 tier: 2/200; P3 and P4 together:
29/671. Keep decision-makers on the list, but do not give P1 for title alone, and give every IN
account at least one route-in below C-level (programme, clinical, practitioner or partnerships
lead) when the export has one. Part of the gap is C-level people not accepting strangers'
invites; the rates are per invite.

**PPL-2 [directional] The referral ask is a way in.** `referral` lane: 21/475 replied; buyer
lanes: 21/958. Referral replied at least as often as buyer lanes in 5 of the 6 campaigns that
had both. A non-buyer at an IN account in a relevant function is a referral-lane PASS, not a FAIL.

**PPL-3 [directional] Functions that do not answer.** Per person contacted: marketing 0/52,
retention / CRM / growth 0/44, non-clinical operations 0/55, engineering 1/90. Partnerships, BD
and sales: 6/83, the highest. Clinical operations titles count as clinical, not operations.
Do not fill an account's cap with marketing, CRM or engineering people.

**PPL-4 [directional] Who the positive repliers were.** Of 34 positive repliers, 3 were C-level.
The rest: coaching lead, Tier 3 practitioner lead, obesity consultant, dietitian, clinical
operations lead, head of commercial, regional partnerships manager, director of clinical
programmes, senior director of clinical research, GM health and wellbeing.

**PPL-5 [watch] Stale contacts.** 5/72 repliers had left the company on the list. Checked
2026-10-30: of the four that can be traced, two came from Sales Navigator exports with no role
start date and one from Apollo with a role started in 2009 (a recent leaver). A filter on
Apollo's role start date would have caught none of them, so there is no filter. A leaver who
names a successor is a referral.

## ICP segment (icp-detail.md, verbatim)

### 2. Online Pharmacies / Digital Prescribers (BMI Verification)

**What they are:** online pharmacies и remote-prescribing platforms dispensing GLP-1 / weight-loss medications; нужно верифицировать eligibility (BMI threshold, обычно ≥27 с коморбидностью или ≥30) без визита.

**Buyer titles:**
- Founder / CEO
- Chief Medical Officer
- Clinical Operations Director
- Head of Compliance & Risk
- Head of Clinical Governance
- Product Manager
- CTO
- Telehealth Ops Manager
- Patient Intake / Care Coordination Team

**Company size & revenue:** 50-1000 employees. **$2M+ annual revenue.**

**Geo:** **UK — приоритетный рынок** (усиливающееся регулирование remote-prescribing и GLP-1 eligibility verification), плюс международные telehealth-провайдеры, работающие в UK.

**Business model:** subscription GLP-1 программы, D2C telehealth, insurance-supported obesity care, online prescription/medication delivery, virtual-first clinical care, remote eligibility/onboarding.

**Pain points — Clinical & Compliance:**
- Пациенты занижают/искажают вес и BMI, чтобы пройти eligibility
- Непоследовательные ручные проверки фото
- Ужесточение UK-регулирования remote GLP-1 eligibility verification
- Сложно верифицировать eligibility удалённо в масштабе
- Нужны defensible verification workflows для аудита

**Pain points — Operational & Risk:**
- Высокие объёмы intake перегружают клиническую команду
- Onboarding abandonment, friction от фото на весах
- Ручная верификация замедляет approvals
- Некорректная верификация BMI повышает риск при назначении, юридическую/репутационную экспозицию

**KPIs:** compliance audit pass rate, eligibility screen accuracy, cost per qualified prescription, regulator complaint rate.

**Triggers:**
- Новое регуляторное руководство по online weight-loss prescribing (особенно UK MHRA/CQC-контекст)
- Инспекция / расследование
- Добавление GLP-1 в formulary

**Positioning:** verify BMI внутри order flow — сократить фрод, ускорить approvals, оставаться audit-ready. Лидировать через compliance/defensibility, не через точность как таковую.

**Examples to target (verify status before outreach):**
- UK: UK Meds (existing customer — исключить из outbound), Manual, Numan, Voy, ZAVA, Second Nature, Juniper UK, Pharmacy2U, Boots Online
- International operating in UK: Hims & Hers, Ro, Noom, LifeMD
